Dialog.Dxvk.WarningContent:
⚠ ADVANCED FEATURE — USE AT YOUR OWN RISK

DXVK is an unofficial DirectX-to-Vulkan translation layer.
No support will be provided if a game is not compatible.

WHO SHOULD USE THIS:
• Primarily benefits older DX8/DX9 games (e.g. FFXIV, Morrowind)
• Enables ReShade compute shaders on games that don't support them natively
• Can reduce CPU-bound stuttering in older titles

IMPORTANT WARNINGS:
• Anti-cheat games may ban players using DXVK
• Game overlays (Steam, NVIDIA, RTSS) may conflict or stop working
• Exclusive fullscreen is blocked — use borderless windowed
• First launch will be slow due to shader compilation (improves on subsequent runs)
• Some games may crash or have graphical glitches with DXVK

Do you want to continue?
Dialog.DxvkInfo.Content:
DXVK translates DirectX 8/9/10/11 API calls into Vulkan.

Benefits:
• Enables ReShade compute shaders on older DX games
• May improve performance and reduce shader stutter
• Enables HDR output via dxvk.conf
• Borderless fullscreen recommended over exclusive fullscreen

⚠ Anti-cheat games may ban players using DXVK.
⚠ Game overlays (Steam, NVIDIA, RTSS) may conflict.

Dialog.FullRefresh.Content:
This will clear all caches and re-scan everything from scratch:

• Re-detects all games from every storefront
• Re-scans DLSS/Streamline DLL paths
• Re-detects graphics APIs and engine types
• Rebuilds shader and addon deployment state

Try a normal Refresh first — it handles most issues without the full rescan. Use Full Refresh as a last resort if games are missing, paths have changed, DLSS has been added to a game, or the DLSS section is missing from a game card.

The next couple of restarts may take a few seconds longer while caches are rebuilt.

Do not close RHI while the refresh is in progress — closing early will result in a missing library and the scan will need to be repeated.

Faq.Body.AddingGamesManually: If a game isn't auto-detected, drag and drop its .exe file directly onto the RHI window. RHI will add it to your library and detect its engine type.
Faq.Body.ChooseShaders:
Click the 'Shaders/Addons' button in the toolbar, then 'Global Shaders' to select shader packs. Lilium's HDR shader pack is selected by default. These apply to all games with ReShade installed.

Expand any pack to pick individual shaders — the pack shows a dash when only some files are selected. Use the Profiles panel on the right to save, load, rename, and share named shader selections. Export a profile as a zip to share via Discord.
Faq.Body.DlssStreamline: Games with DLSS or Streamline DLLs have a dedicated section on the detail panel showing version info. Click to update to the latest version. Using the newest versions is recommended for best performance and quality. RHI backs up originals automatically so you can restore anytime.
Faq.Body.DofFix: DOF Fix backports a depth-of-field rendering fix from Unreal Engine 5.7 to games running on UE 5.0–5.6. It appears in the Recommended section on the game's detail panel when supported. Install it alongside RenoDX for the best result.
Faq.Body.FrameLimiters: ReLimiter and Display Commander are ReShade addons that provide precise frame limiting for VRR displays. Install them from the game's detail panel. ReLimiter is recommended as it's developed by the same team as RHI. Set your target FPS in Settings, per-game via the cog icon, or directly in-game.
Faq.Body.FullRefresh: If games are missing, install locations have changed, or DLSS/Streamline files have been added or removed, use 'Full Refresh' in Settings to rescan your entire library from scratch.
Faq.Body.InstallReShade: ReShade is required for RenoDX HDR mods to work. Click 'Install ReShade' on the game's detail panel. RHI automatically downloads and installs the correct version with full addon support.
Faq.Body.Luma:
Luma is an alternative mod framework developed by Pumbo (HDR Den). Depending on the game, a Luma mod may add HDR, DLAA (Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing), game-specific rendering fixes, or a combination of these — check the Info button for details on what each mod offers.

• Completed mods — named Luma mods for supported games, shown on the Luma row.
• Generic Luma — available for all DX11 Unreal Engine games. RHI installs it automatically and applies any game-specific Engine.ini tweaks or launch arguments listed on the Luma wiki.

You can install RenoDX and Luma on the same game — but there's no guarantee they'll work together on every title. RHI will warn you the first time you try to install both.
Faq.Body.NvidiaDriverSettings: RHI can manage per-game NVIDIA driver profiles. These settings are available directly on each game's detail panel:
Faq.Body.OptiScaler:
OptiScaler replaces DLSS/XeSS with alternative upscalers (FSR, XeSS, Intel Arc) or adds/patches frame generation on any GPU. Install it from the game's detail panel when a game has OptiScaler support.

The ⚙ cog on the OptiScaler row opens per-game settings. For the Nightly build channel these include:
• Streamline/DLSS Enabler — deploys Streamline and DLSS Enabler to the game folder for DLSS Frame Generation support.
• Frame Generation — set FG Input, FG Output, FG Nvngx Override, and HUD Fix.
• Additional Settings — DLSS SR/RR preset, render scale, and flip metering.
• Presets — save and apply named setting presets across games.
• Engine.ini Settings (Unreal Engine games) — Dilated Motion Vectors, FSR Crash Fix, FSR-FG Swapchain, Upscaler Plugin.
Faq.Body.RenoDX:
RenoDX is RHI's primary HDR mod framework. The RenoDX row on each game shows what's available:

• Named mods — game-specific HDR mods from the RenoDX wiki, made by the community.
• UE-Extended — for Unreal Engine games without a named mod. Provides native HDR output via a generic UE addon.
• Unity addon — same idea for Unity Engine games. Provides HDR output for Unity games without a named mod.
• RTX HDR — if no mod is available, you can enable NVIDIA's driver-level SDR-to-HDR conversion via the RenoDX ⚙ cog.
Faq.Body.SelectGame: Your games are listed in the sidebar on the left. Click any game to see its details and available actions. Use the filter chips (All Games, Installed, Unreal, etc.) and search box to find specific games.
Faq.Body.Settings: Click 'Settings' in the toolbar to configure defaults for all games:
Faq.Body.SystemTray: RHI can minimize to the system tray instead of closing. Right-click the tray icon to quickly launch recent games without opening the main window.
Faq.Body.UpdatingEverything: Click 'Update All' in the toolbar to update all installed components across all games at once. This includes ReShade, RenoDX mods, ReLimiter, Display Commander, and more.
Faq.Body.VulkanGames: Vulkan games (shown with a 'Vulkan' badge) use a global ReShade layer installed to C:\ProgramData\ReShade. This requires administrator privileges. When you install ReShade on a Vulkan game, RHI will prompt for elevation.
Faq.Body.WelcomeToRhi: RHI auto-detects your games and lets you install HDR mods, shaders, frame limiters, and manage NVIDIA driver settings — all from one place. Here's how to get started.

Faq.Tip.AddingGamesManually: You can also drag .addon64 files from the RenoDX Discord onto any game to install mods not yet on the wiki.
Faq.Tip.ChooseShaders:
Tip: Per-game shaders can be set using the Shaders button on each game's detail card (when ReShade is installed).
Tip: Use Expand All / Collapse All to browse all packs at once. Deselect All clears the whole selection. Export copies a zip of your selected shaders to the clipboard — paste directly into Discord to share.
Faq.Tip.DlssStreamline: When new DLSS or Streamline versions release, they will appear in RHI automatically. Set your default DLSS preset in Settings. Per-game presets can be changed in the DLSS section on each game's detail panel.
Faq.Tip.DofFix:
DOF Fix only shows on eligible UE 5.0–5.6 games — it won't appear on UE4 or UE 5.7+ titles.
Install and uninstall work the same as any other component.
Faq.Tip.FrameLimiters:
VRR cap presets by refresh rate (leave headroom below max for smooth VRR):
• 60Hz → 59 FPS
• 120Hz → 116 FPS
• 144Hz → 138 FPS
• 165Hz → 157 FPS
• 240Hz → 224 FPS
• 360Hz → 324 FPS
These values are pre-configured in RHI's FPS dropdown menus.
Faq.Tip.FullRefresh: Full Refresh clears the cached game list and re-detects everything. Use it when the normal Refresh button doesn't pick up changes.
Faq.Tip.InstallReShade:
ReShade version can be changed per-game via the game overrides section — choose Stable, Nightly, Legacy, or a custom ReShade DLL.
Vulkan Games: Vulkan games (like Doom Eternal) require admin privileges. RHI will prompt for elevation when needed.
Drag and drop ReShade preset files (.ini) onto a game to install them automatically.
Faq.Tip.Luma:
Luma requires ReShade — it will be greyed out until ReShade is installed.
The Luma ⚙ cog lets you toggle TAA Engine.ini settings for games that need them.
If a game needs a specific launch argument (e.g. -dx11), RHI sets it automatically on install and removes it on uninstall. Launch arguments only apply when the game is launched through RHI.
Check the Info button on the Luma row for game-specific notes — completed mods often include details on what the mod adds or any in-game settings required.
Faq.Tip.NvidiaDriverSettings: Global defaults for VSync, Low Latency, and Power Mode are set in Settings. Per-game overrides are configured directly on each game's detail panel.
Faq.Tip.OptiScaler:
Switch between Stable and Nightly channels per game in the cog — Nightly adds frame generation and additional settings.
OptiScaler and ReShade can coexist. If you see crashes with both installed, try renaming ReShade to a different DLL name using DLL Naming Overrides in the Game Overrides panel.
GPU type and DLSS input settings (AMD/Intel only) are configured in Settings → OptiScaler Settings before installing.
The 'Deploy OptiScaler.ini' button in the cog redeploys your configured INI template to the game folder.
Faq.Tip.RenoDX:
The cog icon next to RenoDX opens advanced settings: Peak Nits, UE-Extended toggle, and RTX HDR configuration.
Engine.ini Settings (Unreal Engine games only): toggle HDR keys and LUT update frequency written to the game's Engine.ini for accurate HDR rendering.
For games not on the wiki, drag and drop an .addon64 file from the RenoDX Discord directly onto the game in RHI.
Faq.Tip.SelectGame: Tip: Double-click a game to launch it directly. Drag and drop a game's .exe file onto RHI to add games not auto-detected.
Faq.Tip.SystemTray: Enable 'Close to System Tray' in Settings to keep RHI running in the background. The tray icon provides quick access to your most recently played games. RHI automatically checks for updates every 4 hours while running, so everything stays up to date.
Faq.Tip.UpdatingEverything: Games with available updates show a green dot in the sidebar. Configure which components are included in 'Update All' from Settings.
Faq.Tip.VulkanGames:
All Vulkan games share the same ReShade installation. Updating ReShade on one Vulkan game updates it for all.
Per-game RenoDX addons and shaders are still installed individually to each game folder.

Info.DisplayCommander: Display Commander is a frame limiter that works alongside ReShade to reduce input lag and improve frame pacing.
Info.Luma: Luma is an alternative HDR mod framework that provides native HDR output for supported games, bypassing the need for ReShade-based injection.
Info.OptiScaler: OptiScaler is an upscaling compatibility layer that enables FSR, XeSS, or DLSS across different GPU vendors, allowing you to use any upscaler regardless of your hardware.
Info.ReFramework: RE Framework is a modding framework for RE Engine games. It enables ReShade injection and other mods by hooking into the game's rendering pipeline.
Info.ReLimiter: ReLimiter is a frame limiter that works alongside ReShade to reduce input lag and improve frame pacing in games.
Info.ReShade: ReShade is a post-processing injector that adds visual effects to games. It is required by RenoDX to apply HDR tone mapping and color grading.
Info.RenoDX: RenoDX is an HDR mod framework that upgrades SDR games to HDR using ReShade. It provides per-game tone mapping and color space conversion.
Info.UeExtended: This game is set to use UE-Extended. It is automatically configured to use native HDR and an Engine.ini will be automatically deployed upon installation. If there is an ingame HDR option then enable that too.

NeuralRendering.Description.Dlss5Tool: For DX12 games with native DLSS. Deploys the DLSS5 Tool ReShade addon and nvngx_dlssnr.dll. Lighter alternative to ShortFuse DLSS Tool when you don't need the full Streamline stack.
NeuralRendering.Description.Dlss5Tool.No: For DX12 games with native DLSS. This game has no detected DLSS — consider ShortFuse DLSS Tool instead.
NeuralRendering.Description.Dlss5ToolBri: For DX11 and Vulkan games with native DLSS. The bridge mirrors the game's DLSS onto a private DX12 session so the NR addon can hook it.
NeuralRendering.Description.Feeder: For games with no native DLSS (DX11, DX12, Vulkan, OpenGL). Feeds a synthetic DLSS contract from ReShade depth and motion vectors. Deploys the Feeder addon, DLSS5 Tool (neural consumer), NR DLL, DLSS SR DLL, and required shaders.
NeuralRendering.Description.Feeder32: For 32-bit games. Feeds a synthetic DLSS contract from ReShade depth and motion vectors. Deploys the Feeder addon, DLSS5 Tool (neural consumer), NR DLL, DLSS SR DLL, and the required shaders (DLSS5_Feed.fx + LumeniteFX).
NeuralRendering.Description.ShortFuse: Recommended for most games with native DLSS. Deploys the full DLSS SR/RR/FG/NR stack and Streamline alongside the ReShade addon. Supports DX12, DX11, DX9, and Vulkan.

NeuralRendering.SfSettings.Description:
When On, RHI will automatically configure ReShade when installing ShortFuse DLSS Tool:
• Rename ReShade to Reshade64.asi
• Install ASI Loader (winmm → version → dinput8)
• Write HookStreamline=1 and HookDirectX=1 to reshade.ini

These steps are needed for FrameGen to work correctly after ReShade.

Note: no longer required on ShortFuse DLSS Tool v0.54 and above.

Setup.Description:
RHI can manage ReShade across all your games automatically. Here's what that includes:

  - Installs and updates ReShade for each game with one click
  - Keeps the correct DLL name per game based on what the game needs
  - Manages shader packs globally - install once, deployed to every game automatically
  - Backs up any shaders already in your game folders before taking over
  - Keeps ReShade in sync when you install RenoDX, OptiScaler, or other components

If you already have a custom ReShade setup - specific shader collections, hand-tuned configs, or a version you prefer - choose "I'll manage it myself" and RHI will leave ReShade completely alone.
